translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: for every natural number m, assuming m ≠ 0, all three conditions hold for d26 m. (1) For every pair of node indices u and v, if u ≠ v, there cannot be both a nonempty chain of dependency steps from u to v and one from v to u. A step from i to j means that there exist two state assignments and a Boolean input such that the assignments agree at every index other than i but give different updates at j on that same input. This condition does not forbid a node from depending on itself. (2) For every node index, its state type is finite and has at most m elements; equality with m is not required by this condition. (3) The number of node indices is exactly one, so the distinct-index condition in (1) is vacuous here.

judgement.summary: For every nonzero natural number m, the target specifies exactly one unit with at most m states, so the prohibition on feedback between distinct units holds vacuously. The passage permits self-dependence in its feed-forward ordering but uses binary components in a three-bit architecture; the single m-state realization is the author’s observation.
